_comment: Real-market benchmarks for the storefront calculator. Each entry is a public asking price or developer price list with the lot area and floor area needed to derive a per-sqm figure. These are ASKING prices, not completed sales - the only market evidence this project has - so they calibrate the band, they do not become an input to any formula.
_policy: numericalAllowed is false for every record. Nothing here enters compute() or computeEstimate(). Their purpose is to prove the market band the multiplier sits in, and to fail the benchmark test if the band moves away from published research.

_bandResearch.statement: Published Batangas research puts ordinary market at 1.5x to 3.0x the BIR zonal value.
_bandResearch.scope: RESIDENTIAL LAND, in desirable locations. Not a province-wide law. Measured against the matched STREET rate rather than a municipal median, the land-only records below land at 1.26x-2.43x (Splendido Taal) and 0.53x-0.68x (Gavina Ville). The band is a calibration target for the middle of the residential market, not a bound the calculator may never cross. It is clamped to this range rather than widened to absorb the outliers, because over-pricing an entire province to compensate for one premium listing is the worse error.
_bandResearch.measuredAgainst: matched street BIR RR rate, not a municipal p50 - a municipal median mixes subdivisions priced far above it with subdivisions priced far below it, so it is not a denominator any individual property can be judged by
sources: https://ren.ph/tools/zonal-value/batangas/batangas-city - 'Market value is not a simple multiplier of the BIR zonal value'

https://richestph.com/batangas-city-real-estate-2024-expert-predictions-and-market-insights/ - 'Actual market transactions in desirable areas often command prices 1.5 to 3 times higher'; residential BIR 500-15000 -> estimated market 750-45000

_referenceBenchmark.source: LandValuePH detailed report LVPH-D-9531904C, dated October 5, 2026 - BINAY ST (RESSURRECCION ST), Poblacion III, Bauan
_referenceBenchmark.inputs: RR 11500/sqm, 100 sqm lot, 120 sqm floor, 2 storeys, mixed CHB, age 6-10, non-corner, TCT

reported.birSchedule: BIR RR 8-2018, as cited by the report

internalInconsistencies: Claimed net factor adjustment is +2.0%, but the four category rows printed in the report sum to +0.5% (land and terrain +0.5, everything else 0.0).
The +2.0% is never applied to the arithmetic: 1150000 x 1.02 = 1173000, not the reported 1350000.
The report's own tax-visibility page states a market rate of 23000/sqm (2.0x BIR), which is inconsistent with the 13500/sqm it actually valued the land at.

Depreciation is labelled '20.0%/year' but 20% is the accumulated figure over a 40-year life, not an annual rate. The remaining-useful-life line states 85% / 34 years, which implies 15% accumulated, not 20%.
The report states active market listing data for Bauan is still being compiled, and shows no comparables. It is a BIR-referenced AVM, not a market-derived appraisal.

records.notes: Greenfield gated township. The 10.16x implied BIR multiple prices a NEW house with clubhouse and full amenities, not ordinary land, so it must not be read as evidence that land is 10x its zonal value. Included to bound the ceiling, not the band.

records.priceBasis: range across models, no lot area published
records.notes: No lot area, so no per-sqm is derivable. Recorded as context only. Never infer sqm from a price range endpoint.

records.priceBasis: publisher shows a per-sqm figure, inside a historical price-trends block
records.priceReliability: low - the publisher shows these rates in a historical price-trends block, not as a current quoted price, and the page does not date them

birStreetCheck.note: measured against the street this project is actually listed on, not the municipal median

records.notes: The single most important record in this file, and it contradicts the model's own premise. Measured against the two BIR street rates that actually cover this subdivision (6000 and 5000/sqm, BIR 035-2022), a 3200-3400/sqm asking rate is 0.53x-0.68x. An established subdivision is priced well BELOW the BIR zonal rate for the same street. The BIR zonal value is a tax base, not a floor on market, so no single multiplier can be right everywhere and the band must be clamped rather than widened to chase outliers. Low reliability because the figure is a historical trend line, not a live quote.
Secondhand house and lot in an established subdivision. Includes a depreciated building, so the land component is below the headline figure.
Small subdivision lot with a house. Small-lot price per sqm runs high, which is why this is not read as a land-only rate.

birStreetCheck.note: Splendido Taal carries different BIR rates per barangay; all three are listed rather than picking the flattering one

records.notes: The only land-only comparable found, and it lands INSIDE the researched band once measured properly. 5270000/310 = 17000/sqm. Against the Dayap Itaas and Niyugan rates of 13500 that is 1.26x; against the Paliparan rate of 7000 it is 2.43x. The earlier reading of 6.8x came from comparing against a Laurel municipal p50 of 2500, which is not the rate this street carries. Gated estate frontage at the Taal recreation belt, so the higher of those two ratios is the relevant end. This record therefore no longer justifies treating the band as an over-estimate.
Listing headline is 10.53M for a 166 sqm lot but the description also offers a 125 sqm house, so the split between land and building is not determinable. Excluded from any ratio test for that reason.
